sections.title: ethos
paragraphs: ethos is a free app for tracking habits, available at manasomali.com/ethos. It is a personal project, run by the person behind the manasomali.com website.
By signing in to ethos, you agree to these terms and to the privacy policy. If you do not agree, do not use the service.

sections.title: Account and access
paragraphs: There is no password. To sign in, you get a 6-digit code by email, valid for 10 minutes and for one use only. Whoever controls your email controls your account, so keep access to it safe.
The account is created on your first sign-in, with the email already confirmed by the code. Each email has a single account. You can end the sessions on all your devices at once.
You are responsible for what is done with your account.

sections.title: Free service
paragraphs: ethos is free and provided as is, with no availability guarantee: it may go offline, change or shut down. There are backups, but there is no guarantee that no data will be lost. To the extent allowed by law, we are not liable for damages caused by downtime, data loss or use of the service.

In the future, ethos may have paid plans, with different features or limits, and ads. Before that happens, these terms and the privacy policy will change, and you will need to accept the new version to keep using the service.

sections.title: Acceptable use
paragraphs: You may not:
request sign-in codes for emails that are not yours, or request codes excessively;
send invites in bulk, to people you do not know or to people who do not want them;
use habit names, notes or invites to send messages, advertising or illegal or offensive content to other people;
try to access other people's data, get around the limits or disrupt the service, for example with excessive automated requests.

sections.title: Limits
paragraphs: To keep the service free and protected from abuse, there are usage limits, including: active or paused habits per person, marks per day on each habit, text length, guests per habit, other people's habits you take part in, invites per day and sign-in codes per hour.
The app tells you when a limit is reached. Limits may change.

sections.title: Sharing
paragraphs: The owner of a habit can invite people who already have an ethos account, either as editors (they mark, unmark and edit marks, including other people's) or as viewers only. The owner controls the habit: only the owner changes its settings, invites, changes roles, removes members and deletes the habit.
All members see all of the habit's content: settings, costs, reward, punishment, marks, notes, history and the emails of the people who take part and of who made each mark.

Members who leave or are removed lose access, but the marks they made stay in the habit. When the owner deletes the habit or their own account, the habit is gone with all of its marks, including the guests' marks, and the guests get an email about it.

sections.title: Blocking and deletion for abuse
paragraphs: In case of abuse or breach of these terms, the account may be blocked or deleted, without prior notice. A blocked account gets no codes and cannot sign in, and its data is kept. A deleted account loses all of its data, as the privacy policy explains, and gets an email about the deletion.

sections.title: Changing your email
paragraphs: The account's email is only changed by support. Send your request to {{supportEmail}} from the account's current email. Before the change, we ask for a reply sent from the new email, to confirm it is correct.

If you lost access to the current email, we may ask for information that only the person who uses the account would know, and we may refuse the change if there is no way to confirm it. After the change, all sessions are ended and both emails get a notice.

sections.title: Your data
paragraphs: What you record in ethos is yours. We use this data only to make the service work. The privacy policy explains what we keep and who can see it, including the service administrator.

sections.title: Not advice
paragraphs: Goals, scores, alerts, rewards and punishments are reminders you set for yourself. ethos does not give medical, psychological or financial advice; for that, see a professional.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: Each version of these terms and of the privacy policy is identified by a date. When a new version is published, the app asks you to accept it on your next visit. If you do not agree, you can delete your account without accepting the new version.

sections.title: Contact
